cases.scenario: Revenue shows a 90% drop for yesterday. The ingest job for the orders source has not completed since the previous morning.
pass_if: Checks pipeline health before interpreting the metric movement
Fires a pipeline alert to the data owner, not a metric alert to the revenue owner
Reports the metric as unavailable for the affected window rather than as a 90% decline
Gives the last good value and its date
Suppresses the metric alert while the pipeline alert is active
fail_if: Reports a 90% revenue decline as a business result
Fires both alerts at equal severity to the same channel
Records the affected period as zero revenue
Investigates segments for a business cause before checking whether data arrived

cases.scenario: A 14-day history of a metric that sits near 100 daily, containing one prior spike of 400. Today's value is 40.
pass_if: Uses median and MAD rather than mean and standard deviation
Flags today's value as anomalous
States that a mean-and-sigma detector would not have flagged it, because the prior spike inflated the standard deviation
fail_if: Computes a mean-based z-score and concludes the value is within range
Excludes the prior spike by hand without a stated rule
Reports no anomaly

cases.scenario: A metric has been exactly 40 every day for 30 days. Today it is 41. MAD is 0.
pass_if: Returns the robust z-score as undefined rather than infinite
Falls back to an absolute-change rule and labels the alert as using the fallback method
Does not emit a critical alert for a one-unit change
Notes that a perfectly constant metric is itself worth a look, since it often indicates a stuck source
fail_if: Divides by zero and emits an infinite or maximum-severity z-score
Returns 0 as the z-score
Crashes the evaluation run

cases.scenario: Daily monitoring is requested on conversions from an ad platform that back-fills conversions for up to 90 days and settles over roughly 28.
pass_if: Excludes the restatement window from metric detection and names the evaluation lag
States plainly that detection latency equals the settlement window for this source
Offers pipeline-health monitoring at one-day latency as the thing that can be fast
Offers the restatement-adjusted series — comparing today's D-1 value against historical D-1-as-observed values — as the route to faster detection
Does not promise next-day detection of genuine metric movement on this source
fail_if: Sets up daily detection on the unsettled window and accepts daily false alerts
Claims next-day anomaly detection on a source that settles over 28 days
Recommends waiting 28 days with no faster alternative offered

cases.scenario: A conversion-count metric averages 3 per day. Today it is 0. A z-score threshold is requested.
pass_if: States that a normal-approximation z-score is the wrong tool at this volume
Computes the Poisson tail probability and reports that 0 is not significant against a mean of 3
Offers aggregation to a weekly grain as the practical alternative
Notes that a min_volume floor should suppress rate alerts on segments this small
fail_if: Reports a 100% drop as a significant anomaly
Applies a z-score threshold that can never fire on the downside without saying so
Refuses to give any assessment of whether today's zero is unusual

cases.scenario: A confirmed anomaly decomposes to a single channel segment that fell 100%. A UTM taxonomy change shipped the same week, renaming that channel value.
pass_if: Checks whether the segment definition changed before concluding the segment moved
Identifies the renamed value and reports the volume as having moved between labels, not disappeared
Uses a full outer join so the vanished and newly appeared segments are both visible
Reports the whole-business figure, which is unaffected
fail_if: Reports that the channel stopped performing
Uses an inner join, so the new segment label is invisible
Escalates to the channel owner for a business investigation

cases.scenario: A request to set up alerting on twenty metrics, with no owner or action defined for any of them.
pass_if: Declines to create alerts with no owner and no action, and explains that an alert with neither is a notification that gets muted
Proposes starting with the two or three metrics somebody will actually act on
Requires a role rather than a person's name as the owner
Sets up the pipeline-health suite regardless, since it has an inherent owner and an inherent action
fail_if: Creates twenty unowned alerts
Defers the whole request until the owner list arrives, delivering nothing
Assigns an arbitrary owner to satisfy the schema

cases.scenario: Monitoring is being expanded from 10 metrics to 200 at the same per-metric threshold.
pass_if: States that false alerts scale with the number of evaluations, so the threshold must tighten
Gives the corrected threshold for the alert budget
Backtests the detector over recent history and reports how many times it would have fired
Recommends against enabling if the backtest count exceeds what a human will read
fail_if: Applies the same threshold at 20x the metric count with no adjustment
Enables all 200 without a backtest
Treats the statistical threshold as fixed regardless of the alert budget
